recto: TEAS 7 Science: scored items per sub-area
verso: Anatomy & physiology 18, biology 9, chemistry 8, scientific reasoning 9 (44 scored; plus 6 unscored pretest items, 60 min), per ATI's TEAS 7 content outline.
Standing upright, facing forward, arms at the sides, palms forward, feet parallel.
Proximal = closer to the trunk or a limb's attachment; distal = farther from it.

recto: Which plane divides the body into right and left parts?
verso: Sagittal plane (midsagittal if the halves are equal).
Frontal: anterior and posterior parts. Transverse: superior and inferior parts.
Negative feedback reverses a change (temperature, blood glucose); positive feedback amplifies it to an end point (oxytocin in labor, clotting).

recto: Which heart chamber has the thickest wall?
verso: The left ventricle: it pumps blood into the aorta for the systemic circuit.
SA node → AV node → AV bundle (bundle of His) → bundle branches → Purkinje fibers.

recto: Which vessels carry deoxygenated blood away from the heart?
verso: The pulmonary arteries (arteries carry blood away from the heart, whatever its O2 content).
CO = heart rate × stroke volume.

recto: Where does gas exchange occur in the lungs?
verso: In the alveoli, by diffusion across the respiratory membrane; surfactant lowers surface tension.

recto: What happens when the diaphragm contracts?
verso: It flattens: chest volume increases, pressure falls, air flows in (inspiration).
Right lung: 3 lobes. Left lung: 2 lobes.
In the stomach (HCl and pepsin).

recto: Where does most nutrient absorption occur?
verso: In the small intestine; villi and microvilli enlarge its surface.
Made by the liver, stored in the gallbladder; it emulsifies fats.
Sympathetic: fight or flight (heart rate up, pupils and airways dilate). Parasympathetic: rest and digest.
Coordination, balance and posture.

recto: Number of cranial and spinal nerves
verso: 12 pairs of cranial nerves, 31 pairs of spinal nerves.
Tendon: muscle to bone. Ligament: bone to bone.
Osteoblasts build bone; osteoclasts break bone down.
Skeletal (voluntary, striated), cardiac (involuntary, striated, intercalated discs), smooth (involuntary, not striated).
Insulin (beta cells) lowers blood glucose; glucagon (alpha cells) raises it.
PTH raises blood Ca<sup>2+</sup>; calcitonin lowers it.
Increases water reabsorption in the kidney's collecting ducts (released by the posterior pituitary).
The nephron: glomerulus and capsule (filtration) → proximal tubule → nephron loop → distal tubule → collecting duct.
The uterine (fallopian) tube.
Epidermis: keratinized epithelium without blood vessels. Dermis: connective tissue with vessels, nerves, follicles and glands.
B cells: humoral immunity, plasma cells secrete antibodies. T cells: cell-mediated immunity, mature in the thymus.
Active: the body makes its own antibodies and memory cells (infection, vaccine). Passive: antibodies received (e.g., across the placenta); short-lived.
Aerobic cellular respiration: makes ATP.
Modifies, sorts and packages proteins.
Prokaryotes have no nucleus and no membrane-bound organelles; eukaryotes have both.

recto: Red blood cell in a hypotonic solution
verso: Water enters; the cell swells and may lyse.

recto: Mitosis vs meiosis: number and type of daughter cells
verso: Mitosis: 2 identical diploid cells. Meiosis: 4 genetically different haploid cells.
Prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase (PMAT), then cytokinesis.
DNA: deoxyribose, thymine, double helix. RNA: ribose, uracil, usually single-stranded.
Transcription: DNA → mRNA in the nucleus. Translation: mRNA → protein at the ribosome.
Start: AUG (methionine). Stop: UAA, UAG, UGA.

recto: Aa × Aa: phenotype and genotype ratios
verso: Phenotype 3 : 1; genotype 1 AA : 2 Aa : 1 aa.
Codominance: both alleles expressed (blood type AB). Incomplete dominance: blended phenotype (red × white → pink).
Amino acids, joined by peptide bonds.

recto: How do enzymes speed up reactions?
verso: They lower the activation energy; they are not used up; heat and extreme pH denature them.

recto: Why don't antibiotics work on viruses?
verso: Viruses are not cells: they have no cell wall or ribosomes for antibiotics to target and replicate only inside host cells.
Gram-positive: thick peptidoglycan wall, stains purple. Gram-negative: thin wall + outer membrane, stains pink.
Atomic number Z = protons. Mass number A = protons + neutrons.
Atoms of the same element (same Z) with different numbers of neutrons.
Ionic: electrons transferred (metal → nonmetal). Covalent: electrons shared (nonmetals).
Solid → gas directly (e.g., dry ice); absorbs heat.
Gas produced, color change, precipitate, heat or light released.

recto: How do you balance an equation?
verso: Change coefficients only, never subscripts, until each element has the same number of atoms on both sides.

recto: Four ways to speed up a reaction
verso: Raise the temperature, raise the concentration, increase surface area, add a catalyst.
M = moles of solute / liters of solution.
C<sub>1</sub>V<sub>1</sub> = C<sub>2</sub>V<sub>2</sub>.

recto: A solution with pH 3 vs pH 6
verso: pH 3 has 1000 times more H<sup>+</sup>: each pH unit is a tenfold change.
Acid: pH < 7, turns blue litmus red. Base: pH > 7, turns red litmus blue.
Independent: changed by the investigator (x-axis). Dependent: measured in response (y-axis).
The group that receives no treatment, used as a baseline for comparison.
Accuracy: close to the true value. Precision: repeated results close to each other.

recto: Which graph shows parts of a whole?
verso: A pie chart.

recto: How to read a graduated cylinder
verso: At eye level, at the bottom of the meniscus.

recto: Metric prefixes kilo, centi, milli, micro
verso: kilo = 1000; centi = 0.01; milli = 0.001; micro = 0.000001 of the base unit.
1 in = 2.54 cm (exact).
